I have grown cotton on this land for thirty years, just like my father did. I know every corner of these 12 mu. Quzhou soil is good for cotton — I have seen it year after year. I will plant all 12 mu to cotton again. That is the only thing I know how to do well, and the cotton traders come to the village every autumn.

I will buy hybrid seeds from the supply cooperative in town. The local ag station pushed those a few years back and my neighbors use them. My yields went up when I switched, so I keep buying them.

For fertilizer, I do what I learned: put down base fertilizer before sowing — a bag of compound fertilizer and some urea — then top-dress twice when the plants are growing strong and when bolls are setting. I do not measure precisely; I go by the bag and by how the plants look. Over the years this works out to roughly 18 kg of nitrogen, 6 kg of phosphorus, and 6 kg of potassium per mu.

My well lets me irrigate, which many in drier parts cannot do. I water before sowing, then during seedling establishment, then heavy during flowering and boll-set, then once more in late summer if it is dry. Four times is my usual.

Bollworm and aphids can destroy a cotton field fast. I spray when I see the moths or when neighbors say the pressure is high. That is usually six or seven times across the season.

I plough every year in spring before planting. My father ploughed, I plough. It breaks up the hard layer and I feel better about the soil.

A good year gives me around 270 kg of seed cotton per mu. Some years less, sometimes more.
